title: Worksheet — Patterns in Mathematics (Class 6 CBSE)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Show your working for the subjective questions; choose the single best option for MCQs. Total time: 30 minutes.

questions.question: The first five SQUARE numbers are:
questions.explanation: Square numbers come from n × n.

questions.question: Two consecutive triangular numbers always add up to a square number.
What is 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 (sum of the first 6 odd numbers)?
questions.explanation: Sum of first n odd numbers = n^2 = 6^2 = 36.

questions.question: Find the next two terms of the Fibonacci sequence: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ____, ____.
questions.answer: 21, 34. Each term is the sum of the previous two: 8 + 13 = 21; 13 + 21 = 34.

questions.question: Find the 7th triangular number using the formula triangular(n) = n(n+1)/2.
Verify that triangular(5) + triangular(6) is a square number, and identify which.
Use the formula 1 + 3 + 5 + … + (2n − 1) = n^2 to find the sum of the first 12 odd numbers.

Draw (in words) a 5 × 5 grid of dots. Mark off L-shaped strips of 1 dot, then 3, then 5, then 7, then 9. Why does each strip have an odd number of dots? What is the running total? What does this prove?
questions.answer: Strip 1 (top-left corner) = 1 dot. Strip 2 (L-shape around it) = 3 dots. Strip 3 = 5 dots. Strip 4 = 7. Strip 5 = 9. Each new strip wraps around the previous square, adding 2n + 1 dots (always odd). Running totals: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 — square numbers. So 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25 = 5^2. The picture proves that the sum of the first n odd numbers is always n^2.

questions.question: Make up your own sequence with a clear rule. Write the first 6 terms and state the rule. Then say which 'famous' sequence (counting/even/odd/square/triangular/cube/Fibonacci/powers) is most similar to yours and why.
questions.answer: Example: rule 'add 4 each time, starting at 2'. First 6 terms: 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22. Most similar to 'multiples of 2 (even numbers)' — both add a constant each time, but mine adds 4 not 2. (Many correct answers; rubric: clear rule + 6 correct terms + comparison to a named sequence.)
questions.explanation: Encourages pattern-creation and connection to named sequences.
